title: Gouraud proclaims State of Greater Lebanon
why: French Mandate adds Bekaa, north, south and Beirut to Mount Lebanon. Today's borders and sectarian arithmetic start here.

title: Constitution of the Lebanese Republic promulgated
why: First constitution, under the Mandate. Sect-based representation enters the text; amended repeatedly, notably 1943 and 1990.

title: Last official census: Christians about half
why: Basis of the Christian-Muslim ratio. No census since; demographics remain politically untouchable.

title: Franco-Lebanese treaty signed, never ratified by France
why: Promised independence in three years; French parliament shelved it. Autonomy talks stall until WWII.

title: Free French general Catroux proclaims Lebanese independence
why: Declaration during WWII; real transfer of power still contested with the Mandate authorities.

title: Unwritten National Pact agreed
why: (date corrected from 1943-10) Khoury-Solh deal: Christians drop French protection, Muslims drop Syrian union; offices split by sect.

title: Bechara el-Khoury elected first independent president
why: Riad el-Solh becomes PM. The Maronite president, Sunni PM pairing is set.

title: French arrest president and ministers; uprising follows
why: Parliament had struck Mandate clauses from the constitution on 8 Nov. Arrests trigger strikes and international pressure.

title: Independence: leaders freed, Mandate ends
why: Lebanon's Independence Day. Nominal only; French troops remain until 1946.

title: Last French troops leave Lebanon
why: Completes independence. Note: one fetched page says French forces left by April 1946; 31 Dec is from memory.

title: Lebanon joins Arab armies in Palestine war
why: Limited Lebanese role; roughly 100,000 Palestinian refugees arrive, the origin of today's camps.

title: Israel-Lebanon armistice signed at Naqoura
why: Sets the frontier line still used. Quietest Arab-Israeli border for two decades.

title: SSNP founder Antoun Saadeh executed
why: After a failed uprising in June 1949; the SSNP becomes a lasting underground force and later coup actor.

title: PM Riad el-Solh assassinated in Amman
why: Architect of the National Pact killed by SSNP gunmen, who were avenging Saadeh.

title: Camille Chamoun elected president
why: Succeeds Khoury, who resigned amid corruption protests. His term ends in the 1958 crisis.

title: Disputed parliamentary elections
why: Pro-Chamoun candidates won 53 of 66 seats amid US support; Chamoun accepts the Eisenhower Doctrine. Tensions sharpen.

title: Egypt and Syria form the UAR
why: Nasserism energises Lebanese Muslims and the opposition; Chamoun sees a threat and leans West.

title: Journalist Nassib Metni killed; revolt erupts
why: Opposition to a second Chamoun term takes up arms; start of the 1958 crisis.

title: US Marines land near Beirut
why: After the Iraqi coup on 14 July, about 14,000 US troops land at Chamoun's request. First Western intervention in Lebanon.

title: General Fuad Chehab elected president
why: Army commander as compromise; one fetched page says August 1958. Takes office 23 Sep; 'no victor, no vanquished'.

title: Karami's cabinet ends 1958 crisis
why: Four-man government splits portfolios evenly; US troops leave by 25 Oct. Crisis toll about 1,000 to 4,000.

title: SSNP coup attempt fails
why: Chehab's army crushes it; the Deuxieme Bureau intelligence service gains power for the decade.

title: Charles Helou elected president
why: Chehabist continuity. The army's intelligence arm loses favour, and Christian parties coalesce against Chehabism.

title: Six-Day War; Lebanon stays out, PLO grows
why: Lebanon avoids fighting, but the defeat pushes Palestinian guerrillas to base themselves in the south.

title: Israel destroys 13 civilian aircraft at Beirut airport
why: Retaliation for an Athens attack. Sharpens the army-PLO divide and Lebanese political split.

title: Cairo Agreement legitimises PLO armed presence
why: (date corrected from 1969-11-03) Legitimised PLO armed struggle from Lebanon and camp control. Lebanese sovereignty complaint for decades.

title: Suleiman Frangieh elected president by one vote
why: Wins 50-49 over Elias Sarkis in parliament; a Chehabist defeat.

title: Black September in Jordan
why: Hussein crushes PLO; by July 1971 its leadership and fighters relocate to Lebanon.

title: Israeli commandos kill three PLO leaders in Beirut
why: Operation Spring of Youth; the government resigns. Armed Palestinian presence becomes a domestic crisis.

title: Army and Palestinian guerrillas clash
why: Two weeks of fighting near camps; the Melkart Protocol follows. Rehearsal for 1975.

title: Sidon fishermen's protest; Maarouf Saad shot
why: Dispute over a fishing monopoly turns deadly. Regularly cited as a prelude to the war.

title: Ain el-Remmaneh bus massacre starts civil war
why: Gunmen kill 27 Palestinians on a bus after an attack on a church event. Official start date of the war.

title: Black Saturday: Beirut sectarian killings
why: Kataeb retaliation for four killed members; roughly 150 to 300 civilians killed at checkpoints. Identity-card killing becomes routine.

title: Karantina massacre and siege
why: Christian militias overrun the mostly Muslim and Palestinian quarter in Beirut.

title: Damour massacre
why: Palestinian and leftist forces storm Christian Damour, in reprisal for Karantina; the town is emptied.

title: Syrian-brokered Constitutional Document
why: Damascus proposes equal Muslim-Christian parliamentary representation; early Taif blueprint. Rejected by both camps.

title: Lt. Col. Ahdab announces TV coup
why: Demands Frangieh's resignation; army splits into sectarian units. The state is hollowed out.

title: Elias Sarkis elected president
why: Elected under Syrian support; takes office 23 Sep. Frangieh refuses to leave until then.

title: Syrian army enters Lebanon
why: (date corrected from 1976-06-01) Syria intervenes on the Maronite side against the PLO-left camp. Start of a 29-year presence.

title: Tel al-Zaatar camp falls
why: After a 53-day siege by Christian militias, with Syria's backing; the camp is razed.

title: Arab Deterrent Force created
why: Riyadh and Cairo summits formalise Syria's presence under Arab League cover. Ends the first phase of the war.

title: Kamal Jumblatt assassinated
why: Druze leader and National Movement head killed near Baaqlin; Druze reprisals kill Christian villagers in the Chouf.

title: Operation Litani: Israel invades the south
why: After the Coastal Road attack on 11 March (38 Israelis killed). Israel occupies up to the Litani.

title: UNSCR 425 creates UNIFIL
why: Demands Israeli withdrawal; the force is still in Lebanon. Resolution 425 is cited in 2000 and again today.

title: Ehden massacre: Tony Frangieh killed
why: Kataeb raid kills Frangieh's son and family; northern Maronite feud shapes later alliances.

title: Hundred Days War in Achrafieh
why: Syrian forces shell East Beirut; Christian opposition to Damascus hardens. Syrian-Maronite alliance ends.

title: Saad Haddad declares 'Free Lebanon'
why: Israeli-backed militia sets up in the border strip; later the South Lebanon Army.

title: Safra massacre: Bashir eliminates Chamoun's militia
why: Lebanese Forces unify Christian East Beirut under Bashir Gemayel by force.

title: Siege of Zahle and Syrian missile crisis
why: Fighting between Syria and the Lebanese Forces in the Bekaa; Syrian SAMs trigger a US-brokered crisis.

title: Israeli air raid on Beirut; PLO truce on 24 July
why: Heaviest raid to that point; US-brokered ceasefire that held until 1982.

title: Israel invades Lebanon (Operation Peace for Galilee)
why: After the 3 June shooting of Israel's ambassador in London; reaches Beirut within a week.

title: Siege of West Beirut begins
why: Israel encircles Beirut for about ten weeks, with heavy bombardment on 12 Aug.

title: David Dodge kidnapped: hostage crisis begins
why: Start of a decade of Western hostage-taking that ends in 1992.

title: PLO evacuation from Beirut starts
why: US, French, Italian forces supervise departure of about 14,000 fighters; ends 1 Sep. PLO leaves for Tunis.

title: Bashir Gemayel elected president
why: Elected under Israeli shadow by a parliament with many boycotts.

title: Bashir Gemayel killed by bomb
why: Killed in East Beirut by an SSNP member; 26 others killed. Israel enters West Beirut.

title: Sabra and Shatila massacre
why: Kataeb militiamen kill civilians in the camps, with the Israeli army controlling the perimeter. Israeli inquiry finds indirect responsibility.

title: Amine Gemayel elected president
why: Brother of Bashir; takes office 23 Sep amid a new multinational force deployment.

title: US embassy bombing in Beirut
why: Suicide truck bomb kills 63; first deadly strike on a US embassy. Islamic Jihad claims it.

title: Israel-Lebanon 17 May Agreement signed
why: Israeli withdrawal tied to Syrian pullout; rejected by Syria and opponents. Cancelled 5 March 1984.

title: Israel leaves the Chouf; Mountain War
why: Druze PSP and Lebanese Forces fight for the Chouf; Christians displaced; US naval shelling at Souq al-Gharb. (date corrected from 1983-09-04)

title: Beirut barracks bombings kill US and French troops
why: Truck bombs kill 241 US and 58 French personnel. US and French forces leave in 1984.

title: 6 February uprising in West Beirut
why: Amal and PSP push the army from West Beirut; the US Marines withdraw. Gemayel's government is crippled.

title: Government cancels the 17 May Agreement
why: Syria's victory; Israel withdraws under 1985 plan.

title: US embassy annex bombing in Awkar
why: Suicide car bomb kills 24; the third bombing in 17 months.

title: Hezbollah publishes Open Letter
why: Formal public debut after years of emergence from Iranian-backed groups.

title: War of the Camps begins
why: Amal, with Syrian backing, besieges Palestinian camps in Beirut and the south for three years.

title: Israel completes withdrawal to the security zone
why: (date corrected from 1985-06-06) Israel pulls most troops back; keeps a border strip run with the SLA until 2000.

title: TWA 847 hijacked; US Navy diver killed
why: Seventeen-day hostage drama in Beirut; Hezbollah-linked gunmen. Robert Stethem killed.

title: Tripartite Agreement signed in Damascus
why: Amal, PSP and Lebanese Forces leaders sign a peace deal; Hobeika is ousted by Geagea on 15 Jan 1986 and the deal collapses.

title: Syrian troops redeploy in West Beirut
why: After Amal-Druze versus Hezbollah fighting; Damascus re-enters the capital.

title: PM Rashid Karami assassinated
why: Bomb on his helicopter; Geagea is later convicted for it.

title: Amal-Hezbollah war in Dahieh
why: Shia rivalry over the southern suburbs; Syria and Iran broker a deal in January 1989.

title: Gemayel leaves office; two rival governments
why: Names General Michel Aoun interim PM; Muslim ministers back Selim Hoss. No president for a year.

title: Aoun declares 'war of liberation' against Syria
why: Months of shelling of East and West Beirut; Iraqi arms support for Aoun.

title: Arab Tripartite Committee ceasefire
why: Paves the way for the Taif talks. [ceasefire announced 22 Sep, in effect 23 Sep 1989 per Washington Post]

title: Taif Agreement signed in Saudi Arabia
why: Signed 22 Oct, ratified 5 Nov 1989. Parity in parliament, cabinet power, Syrian 'special relations'. Ended the civil war politically.

title: Rene Moawad elected president
why: Elected at Qlayaat under Taif; killed 17 days later.

title: President Rene Moawad assassinated
why: Bomb hits his convoy on Independence Day. Elias Hrawi elected two days later.

title: Aoun vs Lebanese Forces: 'war of elimination'
why: Christian-on-Christian war in East Beirut; drains the last resistance to Taif.

title: Constitution amended to implement Taif
why: Parity and cabinet power enter the text; it formally ends the First Republic.

title: Syrian assault on Baabda ends the civil war
why: Aoun takes refuge in the French embassy. Official end of the 1975-1990 war.

title: Dany Chamoun assassinated
why: Killed with wife and sons at home; former Aoun ally.

title: Militias ordered to disband; Hezbollah exempted
why: Cabinet decision; most dissolve by 30 April. Hezbollah keeps arms as 'resistance'.

title: Treaty of Brotherhood with Syria signed
why: Formalises Syria's role; complemented by defence pact in September.

title: Terry Anderson freed; hostage era winds down
why: Last Western hostages released by mid-1992.

title: First post-war parliamentary elections
why: Christian boycott; turnout very low in Christian areas.

title: Rafic Hariri becomes Prime Minister
why: Start of the reconstruction era and of Solidere.

title: Operation Accountability
why: Seven days of Israeli bombardment; 'July War'; an understanding on civilian targets follows.

title: Dahieh protest against Oslo: nine killed
why: Army fires on Hezbollah-backed protesters. [nine killed per partisan source only; another source says 13]

title: Samir Geagea arrested; Lebanese Forces dissolved
why: Held until 2005 amnesty; Christian political exclusion under Syrian tutelage.

title: Hrawi's term extended by three years
why: Constitutional amendment under Syrian pressure; first of several extensions.

title: Israel launches Operation Grapes of Wrath
why: Two weeks of strikes and shelling until 27 April; the April Understanding ends it.

title: Israeli shelling of Qana UN base
why: Kills about 106 sheltering civilians; ends the operation.

title: Army chief Emile Lahoud elected president
why: Sworn in 24 Nov. Term later extended in 2004. Contemporary WRMEA report (Dec 1998) gives 15 Oct; Wikipedia's election page says 13 Oct.

title: Israel completes withdrawal from south Lebanon
why: After 22 years of occupation; Hezbollah claims victory; Shebaa Farms dispute remains. UN Blue Line drawn 7 June.

title: Maronite bishops call for Syrian withdrawal
why: Patriarch Sfeir's statement launches the sovereignty movement that culminates in 2005.

title: Hariri returns as PM after elections
why: Hariri returns to a Lahoud-era cabinet.

title: UNSCR 1559 demands Syrian withdrawal and militia disarmament
why: Fifteen-member vote; Syria and Hezbollah defy it. It is the origin of the Hezbollah disarmament file.

title: Parliament extends Lahoud's term by three years
why: Under Syrian pressure; Hariri resigns 20 Oct.

title: Marwan Hamadeh survives car bomb
why: Anti-Syrian MP wounded; bodyguard killed.

title: Rafic Hariri assassinated in Beirut
why: Truck bomb on the seafront kills the ex-PM and 21 others.

title: Hezbollah-led pro-Syria rally
why: Huge rally; counter-rally on 14 March draws about a million. The March 8 versus March 14 divide is set.

title: March 14 rally: about one million demand Syrian exit
why: Cedar Revolution's peak; government had fallen on 28 Feb.

title: Last Syrian troops leave Lebanon
why: Ends a 29-year military presence; withdrawal ran 26 to 30 April. Intelligence legacy remains.

title: Journalist Samir Kassir killed
why: Car bomb in Achrafieh; critic of Syria.

title: Former communist leader George Hawi killed
why: Car bomb in Beirut.

title: Samir Geagea freed by amnesty
why: Released after 11 years in prison; Hariri bloc cabinet follows with Siniora as PM.

title: Gebran Tueni killed by car bomb
why: An-Nahar editor and MP; UN inquiry expands.

title: Aoun-Hezbollah Mar Mikhael understanding
why: Christian-Shia alliance that shapes later politics and the 2016 election.

title: Hezbollah capture of soldiers triggers July War
why: Israeli air and ground offensive; 34 days; UNSCR 1701 passes on 11 Aug, ceasefire 14 Aug.

title: Shia ministers resign from Siniora cabinet
why: Opposition demands veto power; starts the political crisis.

title: Minister Pierre Gemayel assassinated
why: Kataeb leader shot in Jdeideh.

title: Opposition sit-in begins in downtown Beirut
why: Hezbollah, Amal and Aounists camp at Riad al-Solh; lasts 18 months.

title: Strike turns to Sunni-Shia street clashes
why: Clashes in Beirut; first lethal sectarian violence since 1990.

title: Nahr al-Bared camp battle begins
why: Army fights Fatah al-Islam; camp falls 2 Sep; about 31,000 Palestinians flee and the camp is destroyed.

title: MP Walid Eido killed
why: Car bomb; MP from Hariri bloc.

title: MP Antoine Ghanem killed
why: Kataeb MP; parliament's March 14 majority narrows.

title: Lahoud leaves office; no successor elected
why: Start of a six-month vacuum; parliament postponed the vote dozens of times.

title: General Francois al-Hajj killed
why: Army operations chief who led Nahr al-Bared; car bomb.

title: Intelligence officer Wissam Eid killed
why: Investigated phone data in the Hariri case; car bomb.

title: 7 May: Hezbollah takes West Beirut
why: After the government moves against its telecom network; about one week of fighting.

title: Doha Agreement ends crisis
why: Gives opposition a veto third in cabinet; Suleiman elected on 25 May.

title: Michel Suleiman elected president
why: Army commander elected; ends the vacuum.

title: Special Tribunal for Lebanon opens in The Hague
why: UN-backed court to try Hariri killers; later convicts Salim Ayyash in absentia (2020).

title: Parliamentary elections; March 14 wins
why: Hariri forms a unity government in November.

title: Israel-Lebanon border clash near Adaisseh
why: Dispute over tree trimming; first lethal clash since 2006.

title: Hezbollah-led ministers resign; Hariri government falls
why: Over the STL indictments; Najib Mikati's cabinet forms in June.

title: Bab al-Tabbaneh-Jabal Mohsen clashes flare in Tripoli after Syrian uprising
why: Alawite Jabal Mohsen versus Sunni Bab al-Tabbaneh; repeated rounds until 2014. (corrected from 2011-06 and 'clashes start'; the rivalry dates from 2008, the 17 June 2011 clashes were the first major flare-up after the uprising)

title: STL issues indictments against four Hezbollah members
why: Indictments against four Hezbollah members; confirmed 28 June, made public 30 June. Hezbollah rejects the court. Convictions followed in 2020.

title: Baabda Declaration: Lebanon to stay out of Syria
why: Adopted at national dialogue; Hezbollah's entry into Syria undermines it.

title: Intelligence chief Wissam al-Hassan killed
why: Car bomb in Achrafieh; accusations at Syria.

title: Nasrallah confirms Hezbollah fighting in Syria
why: Qusayr offensive; Syrian war spills into Lebanon.

title: Parliament extends own term by 17 months
why: Election postponed; extended again in 2014 to June 2017.

title: Abra clashes: army versus Assir
why: Sheikh Ahmad al-Assir's group in Sidon fights the army; about 18 soldiers killed.

title: Rweiss bombing in Dahieh
why: Car bomb in Hezbollah stronghold; one of a series, including 2014.

title: Twin mosque bombings in Tripoli
why: Sunni Taqwa and Salam mosques; deadliest attack since war.

title: Iranian embassy bombing in Beirut
why: Double suicide bombing; Abdullah Azzam Brigades claim it.

title: Former minister Mohamad Chatah assassinated
why: Car bomb downtown; Hariri adviser.

title: Tammam Salam cabinet formed
why: After ten months of deadlock.

title: Suleiman's term ends; presidency vacant
why: Vacuum lasts 29 months; parliament fails dozens of times to elect.

title: ISIS and Nusra attack Arsal; soldiers abducted
why: Battle of Arsal; around 30 soldiers and police seized; some killed, some freed in 2015.

title: Parliament extends term to June 2017
why: Second extension; legitimacy of institutions questioned.

title: You Stink garbage protests peak
why: Mass rallies over waste crisis; first civic movement to challenge the ruling class. (corrected from 2015-08-22) [corrected from 2015-08-22: 22 Aug was first large rally (~18,000); mass peak rally ~250,000 was 29 Aug 2015]

title: Burj al-Barajneh twin bombings
why: ISIS suicide attacks in a Shia suburb.

title: Nusra frees 16 captive soldiers
why: Part of the Arsal hostage swap with prisoners.

title: Qaa suicide bombings
why: Eight bombers hit a Christian border village; five civilians killed.

title: Michel Aoun elected president after 46 sessions
why: Ends the vacuum; Hariri returns as PM on 3 Nov after Geagea and Hariri backing.

title: New electoral law: proportional representation
why: Introduces proportional voting with 15 districts and preferential votes; term extended for 11 months.

title: Fajr al-Joroud offensive against ISIS
why: Army and Hezbollah operate on the Syrian border; ISIS leaves on 28 August.

title: Hariri announces resignation from Riyadh
why: Suspended 21 Nov, rescinded 5 Dec after French mediation.

title: First parliamentary elections since 2009
why: Hezbollah and allies gain; turnout about 49 percent.

title: Israel launches Operation Northern Shield
why: Targets cross-border tunnels from Lebanon.

title: Hariri forms cabinet after nine months
why: Longest pre-2020 formation delays.

title: Israeli drones hit Dahieh; Avivim strike follows
why: Hezbollah strikes at an Israeli vehicle on 1 September; limited exchange.

title: 17 October protests erupt nationwide
why: Endpoint of this window; economic collapse and protests follow.
